title: Chow's lemma over a Noetherian base
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme and $f:X\to S$ a separated morphism of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then there exist an integer $n\ge0$, a scheme $X'$, a morphism $\pi:X'\to X$ which is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and an immersion $X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] into $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] such that the composite $X'\to\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ equals $f\circ\pi$; moreover these can be chosen so that there is a dense open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), Section 'Chow's Lemma'; EGA II Theorem 5.6.1(a)

proof.text: *Noetherian conventions.* Every scheme $T$ occurring below comes with a morphism $T\to S$ of finite type: $X$ by hypothesis, the projective spaces $\mathbf P^r_S$ and their closed subschemes because they are proper over $S$ [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper, lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c),(a), and open subschemes $W\subseteq T$ of these, which are quasi-compact in all cases where we use them (see below) and locally of finite type over $T$ (an open immersion is locally of finite type) [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). Hence each such $T$ that is quasi-compact is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; an open subscheme of a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-separated, and an intersection of finitely many quasi-compact opens of a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A morphism from a quasi-compact scheme to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1). If $X=\emptyset$ take $X'=\emptyset$, $n=0$, $U=\emptyset$; so assume $X\neq\emptyset$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, first paragraph (Morphisms 01T6, 01T8; Properties 01OY, 01P0)

proof.text: *An affine cover through the generic points.* $X$ is Noetherian (step 1), hence has finitely many irreducible components [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] and is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [lemma-nagata-dense-affine-cover-exists] (Stacks Properties 01ZX applied at each point, plus quasi-compactness) there is a finite affine open covering $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$, $m\ge1$, such that every $U_i$ contains all generic points of the irreducible components of $X$, and $U:=U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m$ is a dense open of $X$. $U$ is quasi-compact, as a finite intersection of affine opens in the quasi-separated $X$ (step 1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, second paragraph (Properties 0BA8, 01ZX)

proof.text: *Reduction to $U$ scheme-theoretically dense.* Let $c:X^*\to X$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of $U$ in $X$ and $U_i^*=X^*\cap U_i$. By [lem-chow-scheme-theoretic-closure] $c$ is a surjective closed immersion and an isomorphism over $U$, $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X^*$, each $U_i^*$ is affine and $U_1^*\cap\dots\cap U_m^*=U$. The composite $f\circ c$ is separated and of finite type (a closed immersion is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c), composites (a),(e)), and $U$ is dense in $X^*$ (its closure in $X^*$ is $X^*\cap\overline U=X^*$). Suppose the conclusion is proved for $f\circ c$ with the cover $(U_i^*)$, with dense open $U$: a proper surjective $\pi^*:X'\to X^*$, an immersion $\iota:X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ with $p\circ\iota=f\circ c\circ\pi^*$, and $(\pi^*)^{-1}(U)\to U$ an isomorphism. Then $\pi=c\circ\pi^*$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a),(c) and surjective (a composite of surjective maps [def-weil-surjective-morphism]), $p\circ\iota=f\circ\pi$, and $\pi^{-1}(U)=(\pi^*)^{-1}(c^{-1}(U))\to c^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a composite of two isomorphisms. So from now on $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, third paragraph (Morphisms 01R7, 01RB)

proof.text: *Conventions on scheme-theoretic density.* Let $w:W\to T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] (1) the ideal of the scheme-theoretic image of $w$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] on an affine open $V\subseteq T$ is $\ker(\mathcal O_T(V)\to\mathcal O_W(W\cap V))$; so $W$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $T$ (its scheme-theoretic image is $T$) iff $\mathcal O_T\to w_*\mathcal O_W$ is injective, i.e. iff $w$ is scheme-theoretically dense in the sense of [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open] (scheme-theoretically dominant). Injectivity of a map of sheaves is inherited by restriction to an open $T'\subseteq T$; hence if $W\subseteq T$ is scheme-theoretically dense and $T'\subseteq T$ is open with $W\subseteq T'$, and $W\to T'$ is quasi-compact, then $W$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $T'$. In what follows $W$ will be $U$, which is quasi-compact, and $T'$ will be an open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme, which is quasi-separated, so $W\to T'$ is quasi-compact (step 1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, fifth paragraph ('it is also scheme theoretically dense in the open subscheme'; Morphisms 01RB, 01R8)

proof.text: *Immersions of the $U_i$ into projective spaces.* Each $U_i$ is affine, hence quasi-affine, and $U_i\to X\xrightarrow{f}S$ is locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). By [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space-exists] there is an immersion $U_i\to\mathbb A^{n_i}_S$ over $S$, and composing it with the open immersion $\mathbb A^{n_i}_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ over $S$ of [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] gives an immersion $j_i:U_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ over $S$ (composite of immersions [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e)), where $\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ is the projective space of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. (Stacks obtains $j_i$ from Morphisms 01VS, $\mathcal O_{U_i}$ being ample on the affine $U_i$; the closed nodes used here give the same conclusion.) Since $U_i$ is quasi-compact and $\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-separated (step 1), $j_i$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, fourth paragraph, first sentence (Morphisms 01VS)

proof.text: *Closed models $Z_i$.* Apply [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] to the quasi-compact immersion $j_i$: with $Z_i:=\operatorname{SIm}(j_i)\subseteq\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ its scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], a closed subscheme, $j_i$ factors as $U_i\xrightarrow{j_i^{\mathrm{im}}}Z_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ with $j_i^{\mathrm{im}}$ a quasi-compact open immersion. We identify $U_i$ with the open subscheme $j_i^{\mathrm{im}}(U_i)$ of $Z_i$. $Z_i\to S$ is proper: the closed immersion $Z_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ is proper and $\mathbf P^{n_i}_S\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a),(c), [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, fourth paragraph, second and third sentences (Morphisms 01RG, 01WC)

proof.text: *The product and the Segre embedding.* Put $P:=\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $\mathrm{pr}_i:P\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$, and $N:=\prod_i(n_i+1)-1$. By [lem-chow-segre] the Segre morphism $\mathbf P^a_S\times_S\mathbf P^b_S\to\mathbf P^{(a+1)(b+1)-1}_S$ is a closed immersion; by induction on $m$, using that a base change of a closed immersion (here along a projection of a fibre product over $S$) is a closed immersion and composites of closed immersions are closed immersions [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b),(e), there is a closed immersion $\sigma:P\to\mathbf P^N_S$ over $S$. Hence $P\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a),(c), [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], so $P$ is Noetherian (step 1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, sixth paragraph, last two sentences (Constructions 01WD)

proof.text: *The diagonal model $Z$.* Let $j=(j_1|_U,\dots,j_m|_U):U\to P$. Since $j_1|_U$ is the composite of the open immersion $U\subseteq U_1$ with the immersion $j_1$, it is an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e), so $j$ is an immersion by [lem-chow-tuple-immersion]; it is quasi-compact since $U$ is quasi-compact and $P$ quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1). By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], with $Z:=\operatorname{SIm}(j)\subseteq P$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], $j$ factors as $U\xrightarrow{j^{\mathrm{im}}}Z\hookrightarrow P$ with $j^{\mathrm{im}}$ a quasi-compact open immersion whose image is scheme-theoretically dense in $Z$; we identify $U$ with this open subscheme of $Z$. $Z\to S$ is proper (closed immersion followed by the proper $P\to S$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a),(c)), so $Z$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-separated (step 1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, fourth paragraph, display of $j$ and the sentence after it (Morphisms 01RG)

proof.text: *The projections $p_i:Z\to Z_i$.* Let $Z_i':=\mathrm{pr}_i^{-1}(Z_i)=Z_i\times_{\mathbf P^{n_i}_S}P$, a closed subscheme of $P$ (base change of a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b), [def-pc-fibre-product]). Since $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ j=j_i|_U$ factors through $Z_i$, $j$ factors through $Z_i'$ by the universal property of the fibre product; hence every local section of the ideal of $Z_i'$ is killed by $j^\#$, i.e. the ideal of $Z'_i$ is contained in $\ker(\mathcal O_P\to j_*\mathcal O_U)$, which is the ideal of $Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] (1). Applying [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] (2) to the quasi-compact closed immersion $Z\to P$ (whose kernel ideal is the ideal of $Z$) shows that $Z\to P$ factors through $Z'_i$. Hence $\mathrm{pr}_i|_Z$ factors through $Z_i$: there is $p_i:Z\to Z_i$ with $(Z_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_S)\circ p_i=\mathrm{pr}_i|_Z$, a morphism over $S$. Composed with the closed immersion $Z_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$, which is a monomorphism ([lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] (2), uniqueness), both $p_i|_U$ and $U\subseteq U_i\subseteq Z_i$ give $j_i|_U$; so $p_i|_U$ is the inclusion $U\subseteq U_i$. Finally $p_i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], since $Z\to S$ is proper and $Z_i\to S$ is separated (step 6).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, fourth paragraph, from 'Consider the $i$th projection' to 'for example' (Morphisms 01R9, 01W6)

proof.text: *The scheme $X'$ and its immersion.* Put $V_i:=p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq Z$, open, and $X':=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_m$, an open subscheme of $Z$; by step 9, $U\subseteq V_i$ for every $i$, so $U\subseteq X'$. The composite $\iota:X'\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow P\xrightarrow{\sigma}\mathbf P^N_S$ of an open immersion and two closed immersions is an immersion over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e) [def-weil-closed-immersion]; set $n:=N$. Moreover $p_i|_{V_i}:V_i\to U_i$ is the base change of the proper $p_i$ along the open immersion $U_i\subseteq Z_i$ ($V_i=U_i\times_{Z_i}Z$), hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, fifth paragraph

proof.text: *Gluing to $\pi:X'\to X$.* For each $i$ let $q_i:V_i\to X$ be $p_i|_{V_i}$ followed by the inclusion $U_i\subseteq X$; it is a morphism over $S$, because $j_i$ is over $S$ and $p_i$ is over $S$. For $i,k$ the open $V_i\cap V_k\subseteq Z$ contains $U$, and $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in it (step 8 and step 4). The two morphisms $q_i|_{V_i\cap V_k}$, $q_k|_{V_i\cap V_k}$ into $X$ are morphisms over $S$, $f$ is separated, and both restrict on $U$ to the inclusion $U\subseteq X$ (step 9); by [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] they are equal. Since morphisms of schemes glue along an open cover of the source, there is a unique $\pi:X'\to X$ with $\pi|_{V_i}=q_i$; $\pi|_U$ is the inclusion $U\subseteq X$, and $f\circ\pi$ is the structure morphism $X'\to S$, which equals $p\circ\iota$ with $p:\mathbf P^N_S\to S$ since all morphisms of step 10 are over $S$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, sixth paragraph (Morphisms 01RH)

proof.text: *$\pi$ is separated, and $\pi^{-1}(U_i)=V_i$.* $X'\to S$ is separated: it is the open immersion $X'\subseteq Z$, separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] (a), followed by the proper, hence separated, $Z\to S$ (composite [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e)). As $f\circ\pi$ is this morphism, $\pi$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] (b); likewise the restriction $\pi_i:\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is separated, since $(U_i\subseteq X)\circ\pi_i=\pi\circ(\pi^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq X')$ is a composite of separated morphisms. As $\pi|_{V_i}=q_i$ lands in $U_i$, $V_i\subseteq\pi^{-1}(U_i)$; let $e_i:V_i\to\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ be the open immersion. Then $\pi_i\circ e_i=p_i|_{V_i}$ is proper (step 10) and $\pi_i$ is separated, so $e_i$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated]. The image of $e_i$ contains $U$, which is scheme-theoretically dense in the open $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ of $Z$ (step 8 and step 4). By [lemma-nagata-proper-open-dense-iso] $e_i$ is an isomorphism: $V_i=\pi^{-1}(U_i)$, and $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is the proper morphism $p_i|_{V_i}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, seventh paragraph (Morphisms 01W6)

proof.text: *$\pi$ is proper.* The $U_i$ form an open cover of $X$ and each restriction $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is proper (step 12); by [lemma-nagata-projective-target-local] $\pi$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, eighth paragraph (Morphisms 01W2)

proof.text: *$\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism.* Since $\pi|_U$ is the inclusion, $U\subseteq\pi^{-1}(U)$; let $e:U\to\pi^{-1}(U)$ be this open immersion and $\pi_U:\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ the restriction of $\pi$, so $\pi_U\circ e=\mathrm{id}_U$, which is proper (an isomorphism is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c)). $\pi_U$ is separated, as in step 12 [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation], so $e$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated]. Its image $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in the open $\pi^{-1}(U)$ of $Z$ (steps 8, 4), so $e$ is an isomorphism by [lemma-nagata-proper-open-dense-iso], and $\pi_U=e^{-1}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), proof, last paragraph (Morphisms 01W6)

proof.text: *$\pi$ is surjective, and conclusion.* $\pi$ is proper, hence universally closed and in particular a closed map [def-weil-proper-morphism]; so $\pi(X')$ is closed in $X$, and it contains $U$ ($\pi|_U$ is the inclusion), which is dense in $X$ (step 2). Hence $\pi(X')=X$: $\pi$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. (Stacks leaves this to the reader.) Together, $n=N$, $X'$, the proper surjective $\pi$, the immersion $\iota:X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ with $p\circ\iota=f\circ\pi$ (step 11) and the dense open $U$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ an isomorphism (step 14) prove the lemma for $X$ with $U$ scheme-theoretically dense, hence in general by step 3.
